rationale: Independent audit of Package 110 R1 across cycles 1-15 resolves the fixed-load damage evolution mechanism: (1) Imposed boundary displacement was verified as identically u_RP = 0.001966107 mm across all 15 cycles (u2 = 0.0055 mm in Turn 194 narrative was a typographical reference to the global full-scale specimen peak); (2) Damage evolution exhibited a clear inflection at Cycle 5, where initial numerical relaxation contracted Delta d from 0.0500 to 0.01315, followed by accelerating crack propagation from Cycle 6 to 15 (Delta d expanded to 0.02955, RF2 dropped by -10.23% vs donor); (3) Total potential energy decreased strictly monotonically across all 15 cycles (dE_tot = -0.792 uJ < 0), driven by elastic energy release (dE_elas = -20.35 uJ) exceeding fracture dissipation (dE_frac = +19.55 uJ), proving that static energy minimization at fixed displacement naturally drives dynamic crack separation; (4) The driver improperly accumulated history across AM cycles (h_val = max(prev_h, pos_m)), creating an artificial constitutive ratchet where crack-tip strain concentration surged max psi+ from 8.46 GPa to 47.89 GPa and expanded donor history exceedance from 9.77% to 22.35% of integration points; (5) Cycle 5 cannot be declared an authentic verified equilibrium (terminal Delta d = 0.01315 > 1e-3, Delta RF2 = -0.851 N > 0.1 N); the five-cycle cutoff artificially suppressed damage evolution. Gate C1-1 remains PROVISIONAL and Gate C1-2 is NOT QUALIFIED.

scientific_decision.explanation: Cycle 5 satisfies provisional force continuity (-1.66%) and energy continuity (+0.64%) but fails stationarity criteria. It is an arbitrary cutoff of an unconstrained descending energy path. Unconstrained static AM at fixed load cannot track softening equilibrium; advancing to Gate C1-2 requires controlled incrementation with step-frozen history.
scientific_decision.forward_strategy: Implement load-incrementation continuation with authentic step-level history freezing H_n = max(H_{n-1}, psi+(u_n)) at increment boundaries, avoiding intra-increment history ratcheting.
